title: Jail Management System RFQ

onscreen_lines.note: Proposed JMS Secure cloud and only cloud based operation on County-approved computers. Responsive mobile access for tablets and smartphones. Support for current Windows operating systems and commonly used web browsers. • Configurable dashboards based on user role. • Search capabilities across inmate, booking, charge, court, housing, incident, and release records. • Role-based permissions and least-privilege access. • Multi-factor authentication. • Complete audit logs showing users, dates, times, changes, views, exports, and administrative actions. • Electronic signatures, approval workflows, and configurable forms. • Document and image attachment capabilities. • Barcode, wristband, or QR-code support. • Automatic alerts, reminders, and task assignments. • High availability, backup, disaster recovery, and business-continuity protections. • Separate test and production environments. • Configurable workflows without requiring extensive custom programming. • Data export in commonly used formats. • Accessibility features for users with disabilities. Booking and Intake The system should support: • Pre-booking and arresting-agency information. • Identity verification and duplicate-person detection. • Demographic information and aliases. • Photographs, scars, marks, tattoos, and identifying characteristics. • Charges, warrants, holds, bonds, sentences, and court information. • Property and money inventory. • Electronic intake forms and signatures. • Medical, mental-health, suicide-risk, and vulnerability screening. • Keep-separate, protective-custody, PREA-related, and security alerts. • Fingerprint and mugshot-system integration. • Automatic generation of inmate identification numbers and wristbands. • Arresting and transporting officer information. • Intoxication, injury, medication, and special-needs documentation. • Automated booking checklists and supervisor approvals. Inmate Classification and Housing The system should provide: • Objective and configurable classification tools. • Initial and reassessment workflows. • Risk levels and scoring. • Housing recommendations based on classification, gender, charges, medical needs, separation requirements, and available beds. • Real-time housing and bed availability. • Cell, bunk, pod, and unit assignments. • Inmate movement tracking. • Temporary movement and scheduled destination tracking. • Administrative segregation, disciplinary segregation, protective custody, and special-management status. • Historical housing and movement records. • Headcounts and emergency rosters. Advanced Court Liaison Module The court liaison function is a priority and should include: • Centralized court calendar for all inmates and participating courts. • Court dates, times, locations, judges, case numbers, charges, and hearing types. • Import or electronic receipt of court settings, orders, warrants, commitments, and disposition information. • Automatic identification of inmates scheduled for court. • Configurable daily court lists and transportation rosters. • Remote appearance and video-conference scheduling. • Courtroom, equipment, and interview-room scheduling. • Notification of newly scheduled, rescheduled, continued, or canceled court appearances. • Alerts for conflicting court dates or transportation schedules. • Automated reminders for court liaison personnel, detention staff, transportation officers, and supervisors. • Tracking of warrants, bonds, commitments, sentences, releases, detainers, and time-served calculations. • Electronic workflow for receiving and verifying court orders. • Supervisor review when a court order changes an inmate’s custody or release status. • Documentation of court appearance outcomes. • Pending-action queues for orders requiring staff action. • Tracking of paperwork received, reviewed, completed, and returned. • Court document storage linked to the inmate and case. • Secure electronic exchange with courts when supported by the court’s systems. • Calendar views by inmate, court, judge, courtroom, date, and transportation assignment. • Court liaison dashboards showing overdue, pending, conflicting, and completed actions. • Court appearance history and complete audit records. • Automatic daily reconciliation of court schedules against the inmate population. • Reports identifying inmates with no future court date, incomplete dispositions, outstanding paperwork, or possible release issues. • Configurable notification templates for authorized court and justice partners. Vendors should clearly identify which court liaison capabilities are standard, configurable, custom-developed, or dependent on third-party integration. Automated Reporting and Analytics The system should provide: • Configurable automated reports. • Report scheduling by date, time, frequency, and recipient. • Secure delivery through dashboards, protected email, secure file transfer, or other approved methods. • Daily population and headcount reports. • Booking and release reports. • Average daily population. • Length-of-stay analysis. • Charge, bond, court, and sentencing reports. • Housing and bed-capacity reports. • Classification and reassessment reports. • Incident, use-of-force, disciplinary, and grievance reports. • Medical and mental-health activity reports, subject to access restrictions. • Inmate movement and transport reports. • Court appearance, missed court, rescheduling, and pending court-action reports. • Staff activity and compliance reports. • Meal, medication, observation, recreation, and security-check reports. • Billing and per-diem reports for outside agencies. • State and federal reporting support where applicable. • Custom report builder for trained County users. • Dashboards with charts, filters, drill-down capabilities, and export functions. • Automatic distribution based on user role and authorization. • Data export to PDF, Excel, CSV, and other common formats. • Protection against unauthorized disclosure of sealed, medical, juvenile, or otherwise restricted information. The County must retain the ability to create and modify reports without paying the vendor for every routine change. Mobile Capabilities The mobile solution should allow authorized staff to: • Perform inmate and housing searches. • View photographs, alerts, classifications, and authorized record information. • Conduct and document security rounds. • Record inmate movement. • Perform headcounts. • Document meals, recreation, showers, observations, programs, and services. • Create incident and disciplinary reports. • Capture photographs and electronic signatures. • Scan wristbands, barcodes, or QR codes. • Receive court, medical, transport, release, and security notifications. • Work through a secure connection on County-managed devices. • Continue limited operations during temporary connectivity interruptions, if available. • Synchronize offline entries after connectivity is restored. • Remotely disable application access if a device is lost or stolen. Vendors must explain any differences between mobile and desktop functionality. Additional Detention Functions The County prefers a system that also supports: • Inmate property and trust accounting • Commissary integration • Medical and medication records or integration • Incident and use-of-force reporting • Disciplinary hearings and sanctions • Inmate grievances and requests • PREA documentation and tracking • Programs, work assignments, and visitation • Attorney and professional visits • Inmate telephone and video visitation integration • Mail and package tracking • Meal and dietary requirements • Medication pass documentation • Suicide-watch and special-observation checks • Restraint and safety-equipment logs • Transportation scheduling • Release planning and verification • Victim-notification interfaces • Billing for municipal, state, federal, or out-of-county inmates • Inventory and equipment tracking
